newsitem.title: FRANCE: CDR spokesman says no AOM bid for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: CDR spokesman says no AOM bid for Air Liberte.

text.p: French airline AOM does not plan to bid for Air Liberte, a spokesman for state holding company CDR Enterprises, AOM's parent, said on Monday.
"AOM does not propose to buy Air Liberte," the spokesman told Reuters hours after British Airways launched its own bid for the insolvent domestic airline.
CDR is the state entity created to sell off troubled assets of the French bank Credit Lyonnais.
French press reports have identified AOM as a potential white knight for Air Liberte alongside French travel company Nouvelles Frontieres, which says it is considering a bid.
The decision by CDR comes after a British Airways challenge to an AOM takeover of Air Liberte.

On October 4, British Airways, which on Monday bid three million sterling for the assets of Air Liberte, asked the European commission to block an AOM bid for Air Liberte saying that such a bid would be in breach of European Union fair competition rules.
On October 7, the Commission wrote to France to query the sale of Air Liberte, an EU source told Reuters.
